definitions.explanation: Not officially recognized, sanctioned, or announced. Used to describe meetings, statements, or events that lack formal or official status.

examples.japanese: {非公式|ひこうしき}な{会談|かいだん}が{行|おこな}われた。
その{情報|じょうほう}は{非公式|ひこうしき}のものなので{注意|ちゅうい}してください。
examples.english: That information is unofficial, so please be careful.

examples.japanese: {両国|りょうこく}の{首脳|しゅのう}が{非公式|ひこうしき}に{意見|いけん}{交換|こうかん}を{行|おこな}ったと{報|ほう}じられている。
examples.english: It has been reported that the leaders of both countries informally exchanged opinions.

notes:
Composed of {非|ひ} (non-, un-) + {公式|こうしき} (official, formal). The prefix {非|ひ} negates the base word. Functions both as a na-adjective ({非公式|ひこうしき}な) and as a noun.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {非公式|ひこうしき}な{会談|かいだん} (informal meeting/talks)
- {非公式|ひこうしき}な{発表|はっぴょう} (unofficial announcement)
- {非公式|ひこうしき}な{訪問|ほうもん} (unofficial visit)
- {非公式|ひこうしき}に (informally, off the record)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {公式|こうしき} — official, formal (the antonym)
- {私的|してき} — private, personal (focuses on private vs. public rather than official status)
- オフレコ — off the record (journalism term, loanword from English)
